title: Observation of Flat Bands in Type-II Weyl Semimetal TaRhTe$_{4}$
authors: Harry Rankin, Tyler J. Slade, Benjamin Schrunk, Yevhen Kushnirenko, Andrew Eaton, K. U. R. R. S. Rathnayaka, Maxwell Doyle, Lin-Lin Wang, Paul C. Canfield, Adam Kaminski
abstract: Flat bands have been theoretically predicted for decades but have only recently been realized in quantum materials such as magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, kagome and Lieb lattices, and rare-earth metal compounds. To date, only twisted layered materials have enabled tuning of flat-band energies near the electronic chemical potential, thereby influencing transport and thermodynamic properties. Here, we report the presence of flat bands near the chemical potential in bulk TaRhTe$_{4}$, a noncentrosymmetric van-der Waals type-II Weyl semimetal. Flat bands are rarely observed in Weyl semimetals, particularly in nonmagnetic bulk systems, and the observed flat bands were not predicted by density functional theory calculations. TaRhTe$_{4}$ therefore provides a platform in which nontrivial topology coexists with flat bands near the Fermi level, as evidenced by our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements.
summary: This work reports the experimental detection of flat energy bands near the Fermi level in the bulk Weyl semimetal $	ext{TaRhTe}_4$. Using ARPES, the authors demonstrated that these flat bands coexist with the material's topological properties, a finding that was not predicted by standard DFT calculations. This suggests $	ext{TaRhTe}_4$ is a promising platform for studying the interplay between topology and strong electronic correlations.
main_problem: The primary goal was observing flat bands near the Fermi level in a nonmagnetic bulk Weyl semimetal, as such features are rare and unexpected based on initial theoretical calculations.
main_result: The study reports clear evidence of flat bands via ARPES measurements in $	ext{TaRhTe}_4$ that coexist with its nontrivial topological character (Weyl points), despite these bands not being predicted by DFT.
method: The research combines Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) on cleaved single crystals with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to probe the electronic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{TaRhTe}_4$, a noncentrosymmetric van-der Waals type-II Weyl semimetal. Measurements were performed on different crystal terminations (A and B), comparing experimental data against DFT predictions.
key_observables: Flat bands (constant energy over momentum range), Fermi surfaces, Weyl points, and Fermi arcs connecting these points.
important_parameters: The flat band energy was observed near $4 	ext{ meV}$ below the chemical potential ($	ext{E}_F$).
main_assumptions: A key finding is that the observed flat bands were *not* predicted by DFT, suggesting a novel physical mechanism at play.
figures_summary: Figures compare ARPES and DFT Fermi surfaces for two terminations (A and B). Specific cuts highlight the distinct presence of momentum-independent flat bands in Termination A data relative to theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context by noting the rarity of flat bands in Weyl semimetals. It then presents comparative analysis using ARPES vs. DFT, focusing on identifying and characterizing the unexpected flat band features observed experimentally.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state topology, the observation of emergent electronic states (flat bands) that deviate from standard mean-field theory predictions is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated physics in novel quantum materials.

Figure 2: Fermi surfaces of TaRhTe4. a,b DFT-calculated and ARPES Fermi surfaces for termination B. The green and purple icons show the theoretical momentum positions of the Weyl points. The green WP projections have chirality -1 and the purple WP projections have chirality +1. The squares depict WP projections with predicted energy 13 meV above EF , whereas the circles represent WP projections with energy 50 meV below EF . c,d DFT-calculated and ARPES Fermi surfaces for termination A. Note that in this termination, we obtained data out to ky ≈0.25 1/˚A, whereas for termination B, we only obtained data out to ky ≈0.20 1/˚A.

The purple arrows indicate the theoretical locations of the WPs. d-f ARPES-measured energy-momentum cuts through termination B. The white arrows are placed at the same location as the purple arrows in the DFT calculations. g-i DFT-calculated energy-momentum cuts through termination B. j-l ARPES-measured energy-momentum cuts through termination B. 6

Figure 4: Flat bands in the Fermi surface of termination A. a FS of termination A, showing how the flat bands extend throughout most of the Brillouin zone. b,c,d Several energy-momentum cuts in which the flat bands are visible. The flat bands are shown by the white arrows. e EDCs of panel (b), focused on the area enclosed by the smaller white frame. f EDCs of panel (b) without offset. The individual EDCs are colored distinctly only to highlight that the peaks occur at the same energy for each EDC. The peak of the flat bands occurs approximately 4 meV below the Fermi energy.
